claim: pmk1Δ and sty1Δ cells are extremely sensitive to thiabendazole (TBZ), while spk1Δ cells are not.
source: We noticed that pmk1∆ and sty1∆ but not spk1∆ cells were extremely sensitive to TBZ
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from serial dilution assays shown in Figure 1B, which demonstrate differential sensitivity of MAPK deletion mutants to TBZ.

claim: Constitutively activated CIP or SAP signaling by overexpressing Pek1DD or Wis1DD causes yeast cells to be sensitive to TBZ.
source: constitutively activated CIP or SAP signaling by overexpressing Pek1DD (Pek1-S234D;T238D) (Sugiura et al., 1999) or Wis1DD (Wis1-S469D;T473D) (Shiozaki et al., 1998), respectively, but not activated PSP signaling by overexpressing Byr1DD (Byr1-S214D;T218D) (Ozoe et al., 2002), also caused yeast cells to be sensitive to TBZ
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from serial dilution assays shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, B.

claim: Inactivation of CIP signaling by pmk1Δ or SAP by sty1-T97A compromises full SAC activation, with less than 60% of cells showing Cdc13-GFP on SPBs after cold treatment for 6 hr.
source: We found that inactivation of CIP signaling by pmk1∆ or SAP by sty1-T97A compromised full SAC activation, as these two mutants had only less than 60% of cells with Cdc13-GFP on SPBs after cold treatment for 6 hr, whereas the percentage in wild-type and spk1∆ cells after the same treatment was roughly 90%
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative microscopy data from time-course analyses shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The disappearance of Cdc13-GFP from SPBs when released from metaphase arrest is severely delayed in pek1DD and wis1DD but not byr1DD mutant cells.
source: Consistently, the disappearance of Cdc13-GFP from SPBs when released from metaphase arrest was severely delayed in pek1DD and wis1DD but not byr1DD mutant cells
evidence: The claim is supported by time-course microscopy data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2C, D.

claim: The ability of Mad2-overexpressing cells to arrest in mitosis is compromised in pmk1Δ and sty1-T97A mutants, but not in spk1Δ mutant.
source: We found that the ability of Mad2-overexpressing cells to arrest in mitosis was clearly compromised in pmk1∆ and sty1-T97A mutants, but not in spk1∆ mutant
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: More MCC components (Mad2 plus Mad3 and Slp1Cdc20) are co-immunoprecipitated with APC/C in wis1DD cells compared to wild-type.
source: Compared to wild-type, more MCC components (Mad2 plus Mad3 and Slp1Cdc20) were co-immunoprecipitated in wis1DD cells
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Less MCC components are co-immunoprecipitated with APC/C in pek1DD cells compared to wild-type.
source: Compared to wild-type, more MCC components (Mad2 plus Mad3 and Slp1Cdc20) were co-immunoprecipitated in wis1DD cells, while less of them were co-immunoprecipitated in pek1DD cells
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Slp1Cdc20 levels are significantly reduced in pek1DD but not wis1DD cells.
source: Further analysis of the inputs of these immunoprecipitations showed that Slp1Cdc20 levels were significantly reduced in pek1DD but not wis1DD cells
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2B.

claim: Slp1Cdc20 level is significantly increased in pmk1Δ and pmk1Δ sty1-T79A cells but not in sty1-T79A cells.
source: Consistently, the Slp1Cdc20 level was significantly increased in pmk1Δ and pmk1Δ sty1-T79A cells but not in sty1-T79A cells
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Attenuated levels of Slp1Cdc20 in pek1DD cells are not due to decreased transcription of slp1+ gene.
source: It is noteworthy that attenuated levels of Slp1Cdc20 in pek1DD cells was not due to decreased transcription of slp1+ gene
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: CIP signaling only plays a negligible role in influencing Slp1Cdc20 levels when SAC is not activated.
source: These results suggested that CIP signaling only plays a negligible role in influencing Slp1Cdc20 levels when SAC is not activated.
evidence: The claim is based on immunoblot data from cdc25-22 background cells shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, where only marginally reduced Slp1Cdc20 levels were detected in pek1DD cells and no elevated levels in pmk1Δ cells.

claim: Pmk1 expressed from yeast cells can be pulled down by MBP-tagged Slp1Cdc20.
source: Through incubating MBP-tagged Slp1Cdc20 with metaphase-arrested yeast cell lysates, we found that Pmk1 expressed from yeast cells could be pull-downed by Slp1Cdc20
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Mutating either of the two most N-terminal basic-residue patches (19-KKR-21 and 47-KR-48) to glutamates or alanines in Slp1Cdc20 results in decreased amount of Slp1Cdc20 pulled down by Pmk1-GST in vitro.
source: We found that mutating either of the two most N-terminal basic-residue patches (19-KKR-21 and 47-KR-48) to glutamates (Glu, E) or alanines (Ala, A) in Slp1Cdc20 resulted in decreased amount of Slp1Cdc20 pulled down by Pmk1-GST in vitro using the bacterially expressed recombinant proteins
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro GST pull-down assay data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Mutating both basic-residue patches or mutating only the two arginine residues (R21 and R48) in those patches is sufficient to completely disrupt Pmk1-Slp1Cdc20 interaction.
source: mutating both patches or mutating only the two arginine residues (R21 and R48) in those patches was sufficient to completely disrupt their interaction
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro GST pull-down assay data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Mutations of Pmk1-docking sequences in Slp1 (PDSS) to alanines mimic pmk1Δ mutant in both elevated Slp1Cdc20 protein levels and defective activation and maintenance of the SAC upon nda3-mediated checkpoint arrest.
source: Importantly, mutations of these Pmk1-docking sequences in Slp1 (PDSS for short) to alanines mimicked pmk1Δ mutant in both elevated Slp1Cdc20 protein levels (Figure 3D) and defective activation and maintenance of the SAC upon nda3-mediated checkpoint arrest
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data in Figure 3D and time-course microscopy data in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Insertion of a 15 amino acid sequence of Pmp1 containing the Pmk1-docking sequence (PDSP) in front of the first basic-residue patch in Slp1(DS-5A) mutant protein restores its interaction with Pmk1.
source: Very strikingly, insertion of a 15 amino acid sequence of Pmp1 containing the Pmk1-docking sequence (or PDSP for short) right in front of the first basic-residue patch in Slp1(DS-5A) mutant protein restored its interaction with Pmk1
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro GST pull-down assay data shown in Figure 3B, C.

claim: Bacterially expressed recombinant GST-Slp1Cdc20 can be efficiently phosphorylated in the presence of Pmk1-HA-His purified from yeast cells.
source: we performed in vitro phosphorylation reactions and found that bacterially expressed recombinant GST-Slp1Cdc20 could be efficiently phosphorylated in the presence of Pmk1-HA-His purified from yeast cells
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro kinase assay data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Thr480 of Slp1Cdc20 is a major Pmk1 phosphorylation site in vivo upon SAC activation.
source: Thus, our results established Thr480 of Slp1Cdc20 as a major Pmk1 phosphorylation site in vivo upon SAC activation.
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C–E, and Figure 4—figure supplement 2), in vitro kinase assays (Figure 4C), and in vivo phosphorylation detection (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 3C).

claim: Ser28 and Thr31 in Slp1Cdc20 are phosphorylated by Cdk1 in vitro and in vivo.
source: By using the phospho-specific antibodies against both pS28 and pT31, we could detect the phosphorylation of Ser28 and Thr31 in vitro by Cdc13 (cyclin B)-containing Cdk1 complexes purified from metaphase-arrested yeast cells, which was severely diminished when the kinase activity of ATP analog-sensitive Cdk1 [Cdc2-as1(F84G)] was inhibited by 1-NM-PP1 or when Slp1(S28A;T31A) was added as the substrate in in vitro kinase reactions (Figure 4E). Next, we examined whether Ser28 and Thr31 were phosphorylated in vivo. Slp1Cdc20 was co-immunoprecipitated with Apc15 from nda3-arrested yeast cells and detected with phospho-specific antibodies. We observed phosphorylation of Ser28/Thr31 in wild-type cells, but it disappeared in phosphatase-treated wild-type samples and in 1-NM-PP1-treated cdc2-as1 cells, or when cells expressing Slp1(S28A;T31A) were collected as the substrate
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro kinase assay data (Figure 4E) and in vivo phosphorylation detection (Figure 4F).

claim: Phospho-deficient Slp1T480A mutant shows elevated Slp1Cdc20 levels in both metaphase-arrested and asynchronously grown cells.
source: Indeed, phospho-deficient Slp1T480A mutant showed elevated Slp1Cdc20 levels in both metaphase-arrested and asynchronously grown cells (Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 5)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: Slp1T480A mutant shows compromised SAC activation compared to wild-type cells.
source: phospho-deficient Slp1T480A mutant showed elevated Slp1Cdc20 levels in both metaphase-arrested and asynchronously grown cells (Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 5) and compromised SAC activation compared to wild-type cells, likely due to more efficient APC/C activation
evidence: The claim is supported by time-course microscopy data shown in Figure 4H and Figure 4—figure supplement 6.

claim: Slp1T480A mutant reverses the inhibitory effect of pek1DD on Slp1Cdc20 stability and APC/C activation after release from SAC-mediated arrest.
source: Furthermore, Slp1T480A mutant also reversed the inhibitory effect of pek1DD on Slp1Cdc20 stability and APC/C activation after release from SAC-mediated arrest
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data (Figure 4G) and time-course microscopy data (Figure 4H).

claim: Deletion of apc15 recovers Slp1Cdc20 levels in pek1DD cells.
source: As expected, we indeed observed that deletion of apc15 recovered Slp1Cdc20 levels in pek1DD cells
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Deletion of apc15 lowers the percentage of cells with Cdc13-GFP retained on SPBs in nda3-KM311 pek1DD cells after cold treatment.
source: we indeed observed that deletion of apc15 recovered Slp1Cdc20 levels in pek1DD cells (Figure 5A), and lowered the percentage of cells with Cdc13-GFP retained on SPBs in nda3-KM311 pek1DD cells after cold treatment
evidence: The claim is supported by time-course microscopy data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: K479 is an ubiquitin-modifying site in Slp1Cdc20.
source: During the course of our mass spectrometry analysis on Slp1Cdc20 phosphorylation, we also detected Lys 479 (K479) as an ubiquitin-modifying site
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Mutation of K479 to arginine increases the protein levels of Slp1Cdc20.
source: In agreement with the mass spectrometry analysis, mutation of K479 to arginine indeed increased the protein levels of Slp1Cdc20
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: nda3-KM311 slp1K479R cells demonstrate lowered metaphase arrest rate after cold treatment, indicating defective SAC activation.
source: Furthermore, nda3-KM311 slp1K479R cells also demonstrated lowered metaphase arrest rate after cold treatment (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1), indicating defective SAC activation.
evidence: The claim is supported by time-course microscopy data shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Replacement of K472 with arginine efficiently stabilizes Slp1Cdc20, similar to K479R mutant.
source: Although K472 was not identified as an ubiquitin-modifying residue in our mass spectrometry analysis, replacement of K472 with arginine also efficiently stabilized Slp1Cdc20, similar to K479R mutant
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Simultaneously mutating both K472 and K479 causes additive effects in elevating Slp1Cdc20 protein levels and lowering SAC activation rate in wild-type or pek1DD strain background.
source: Strikingly, simultaneously mutating both K472 and K479 caused additive effects in elevating Slp1Cdc20 protein levels and lowering SAC activation rate in wild-type or pek1DD strain background
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 2) and time-course microscopy data (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).

claim: Mutating both K472 and K479 largely removes the higher molecular weight bands corresponding to ubiquitylated species of Slp1Cdc20.
source: Consistently, using TUBEs (tandem ubiquitin-binding entities) (Hjerpe et al., 2009) to enrich for ubiquitinated proteins in metaphase-arrested mts3-1 cells expressing sfGFP-Slp1, we were able to demonstrate that mutating both K472 and K479 largely removed the higher molecular weight bands detected by immunoblotting, which corresponded to the ubiquitylated species of Slp1Cdc20
evidence: The claim is supported by TUBE pull-down assay data shown in Figure 5E, F.

claim: A much weaker discrete laddering pattern of sfGFP-Slp1 is observed in pmk1Δ cells compared to wild-type cells, indicating reduced ubiquitylation levels.
source: Indeed, we observed a much weaker or stronger discrete laddering pattern of sfGFP-Slp1 in pmk1Δ or pek1DD cells, respectively, than that of wild-type cells, indicating reduced or enhanced ubiquitylation levels
evidence: The claim is supported by TUBE pull-down assay data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: A stronger discrete laddering pattern of sfGFP-Slp1 is observed in pek1DD cells compared to wild-type cells, indicating enhanced ubiquitylation levels.
source: Indeed, we observed a much weaker or stronger discrete laddering pattern of sfGFP-Slp1 in pmk1Δ or pek1DD cells, respectively, than that of wild-type cells, indicating reduced or enhanced ubiquitylation levels
evidence: The claim is supported by TUBE pull-down assay data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Mutations of T480A, S76A/T480A, and Pmk1-docking site reduce polyubiquitylation of Slp1Cdc20 in both pek1+ cells and pek1DD-overexpressing cells.
source: Furthermore, mutations of T480A, S76A/T480A, and Pmk1-docking site, but not S28A/T31A- or S28A/T31A/S59A-containing mutants, also reduced polyubiquitylation of Slp1Cdc20 in both pek1+ cells (Figure 5F) and pek1DD-overexpressing (i.e. Padh11-pek1DD) cells
evidence: The claim is supported by TUBE pull-down assay data shown in Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 5.

claim: Treatment with KCl or caspofungin results in full activation of both Pmk1 and Sty1 (for KCl treatment) or only Pmk1 (for caspofungin treatment).
source: As previously reported, treatment with KCl or caspofungin resulted in full activation of both Pmk1 and Sty1 (for KCl treatment) or only Pmk1 (for caspofungin treatment) as determined using anti-phospho p42/44 or anti-phospho p38 antibodies, which serve as indicative of Pmk1 or Sty1 activation, respectively
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6B and cites previous reports.

claim: Treatment with KCl or caspofungin correlates with a marked and rapid decrease in Slp1Cdc20 levels.
source: Intriguingly, treatment with KCl or caspofungin also correlated with a marked and rapid decrease in Slp1Cdc20 levels
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: SAC activation per se does not trigger activation of CIP pathway.
source: It is noteworthy that SAC activation per se did not trigger activation of CIP pathway, as we did not observe any elevated Pmk1 phosphorylation in metaphase-arrested cells either by nda3-KM311 mutation (see 'control' samples in Figure 6B) or by Mad2 overexpression
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Treatment of fission yeast cells with KCl or caspofungin does not alter APC/C–MCC interaction when cells are treated by caspofungin.
source: Surprisingly, we did not see any alteration of APC/C–MCC interaction accompanying Pmk1 activation when cells were treated by caspofungin
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The high SAC activation efficiency in mitosis-arrested cells exposed to osmotic stress (KCl) or cell wall damage stress (caspofungin) is greatly lowered by pmk1 deletion.
source: Nevertheless, the high SAC activation efficiency in mitotis-arrested cells exposed to osmotic stress (KCl) or cell wall damage stress (caspofungin) was greatly lowered by pmk1 deletion
evidence: The claim is supported by time-course microscopy data shown in Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Pmk1-docking site mutant slp1(DS-5A) and Pmk1 phosphorylation-deficient mutants slp1T480A and slp1S76A;T480A can partially suppress the sustained SAC activation responding to osmotic and cell wall damage stresses.
source: Furthermore, Pmk1-docking site mutant slp1(DS-5A) and Pmk1 phosphorylation-deficient mutants slp1T480A and slp1S76A;T480A could partially suppress the sustained SAC activation responding to osmotic and cell wall damage stresses
evidence: The claim is supported by time-course microscopy data shown in Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Protein levels of Pmk1 phosphorylation-deficient mutants Slp1T480A and Slp1S76A;T480A under osmotic and cell wall damage stresses are restored almost to the levels of wild-type Slp1 in untreated metaphase-arrested cells.
source: Accordingly, protein levels of Pmk1 phosphorylation-deficient mutants Slp1T480A and Slp1S76A;T480A under above stresses were restored almost to the levels of wild-type Slp1 in untreated metaphase-arrested cells
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Stressed pmk1Δ cells display greatly increased frequency of lagging chromosomes and chromosome mis-segregation at mitotic anaphase compared to similarly treated wild-type cells or untreated pmk1Δ cells.
source: We found that stressed pmk1Δ cells displayed greatly increased frequency of lagging chromosomes and chromosome mis-segregation at mitotic anaphase compared to similarly treated wild-type cells or untreated pmk1Δ cells
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data analyzing chromosome segregation defects shown in Figure 7B, C.

claim: The fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe has three MAPK-signaling cascades: the pheromone signaling pathway (PSP), the stress-activated pathway (SAP), and the cell integrity pathway (CIP), with Spk1, Sty1, or Pmk1 as the MAPK, respectively.
source: The fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe has three MAPK-signaling cascades: the pheromone signaling pathway (PSP), the stress-activated pathway (SAP), and the cell integrity pathway (CIP), with Spk1, Sty1, or Pmk1 as the MAPK, respectively (Figure 1A; Cansado et al., 2021; Perez and Cansado, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to established literature (Cansado et al., 2021; Perez and Cansado, 2010) and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Sty1 can phosphorylate kinase Srk1 or Polo kinase Plo1 to negatively or positively regulate Cdc25 phosphatase and thus the onset of mitosis, respectively.
source: Sty1 can phosphorylate kinase Srk1 or Polo kinase Plo1 to negatively or positively regulate Cdc25 phosphatase and thus the onset of mitosis, respectively (López-Avilés et al., 2005; López-Avilés et al., 2008; Petersen and Hagan, 2005; Petersen and Nurse, 2007; Smith et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (López-Avilés et al., 2005; López-Avilés et al., 2008; Petersen and Hagan, 2005; Petersen and Nurse, 2007; Smith et al., 2002).

claim: Sty1 and Pmk1 can pose negative effect on assembly of contractile actomyosin ring and cytokinesis in response to actin cytoskeleton damage or cell wall stress.
source: Recent studies have also demonstrated that Sty1 and Pmk1 can pose negative effect on assembly of contractile actomyosin ring and cytokinesis in response to actin cytoskeleton damage or cell wall stress (e.g. treatment with blankophor, caspofungin, and caffeine) (Edreira et al., 2020; Gómez-Gil et al., 2020)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to recent studies (Edreira et al., 2020; Gómez-Gil et al., 2020).

claim: All genes encoding the major components of three MAPK signaling cascades in fission yeast are non-essential.
source: Intriguingly, all genes encoding the major components of three MAPK signaling cascades in fission yeast are non-essential (Kim et al., 2010)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Kim et al., 2010.

claim: Previous studies have revealed that the active MAPK is required for spindle checkpoint activation and APC/C inhibition in Xenopus egg extracts or tadpole cells.
source: Previous studies have revealed that the active MAPK is required for spindle checkpoint activation and APC/C inhibition in Xenopus egg extracts or tadpole cells (Chen, 2004; Chung and Chen, 2003; Minshull et al., 1994; Takenaka et al., 1997; Zhao and Chen, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Chen, 2004; Chung and Chen, 2003; Minshull et al., 1994; Takenaka et al., 1997; Zhao and Chen, 2006).

claim: Phosphorylation of several components of SAC, including Cdc20, Mps1, and Bub1, by MAPK serves as regulatory signals to block APC/C activation upon SAC activation.
source: These studies suggested that phosphorylation of several components of SAC, including Cdc20, Mps1, and Bub1, by MAPK serves as regulatory signals to block APC/C activation upon SAC activation (Chen, 2004; Chung and Chen, 2003; Zhao and Chen, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Chen, 2004; Chung and Chen, 2003; Zhao and Chen, 2006).

claim: Cdc20 is unique amongst the MCC proteins in that it can function as either a co-activator or an inhibitor of the APC/C.
source: Thus, Cdc20 is unique amongst the MCC proteins in that it can function as either a co-activator or an inhibitor of the APC/C.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about the dual role of Cdc20 in APC/C regulation.

claim: The key SAC components Mad2 and Mad3 and one molecule of Slp1Cdc20 form MCC which binds to APC/C through another molecule of Slp1Cdc20 upon checkpoint arrest in fission yeast.
source: In fission yeast, the key SAC components Mad2 and Mad3 and one molecule of Slp1Cdc20 form MCC which binds to APC/C through another molecule of Slp1Cdc20 upon checkpoint arrest, and the recovery from mitotic arrest accompanies the loss of MCC–APC/C binding (May et al., 2017; Sczaniecka et al., 2008; Sewart and Hauf, 2017; Vanoosthuyse and Hardwick, 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (May et al., 2017; Sczaniecka et al., 2008; Sewart and Hauf, 2017; Vanoosthuyse and Hardwick, 2009).

claim: Apc15, one of the conserved components of APC/C, promotes Cdc20/Slp1Cdc20 autoubiquitylation and its turnover by APC/C in both human and fission yeast cells.
source: It has been shown in both human and fission yeast cells that Apc15, one of the conserved components of APC/C, promotes Cdc20/Slp1Cdc20 autoubiquitylation and its turnover by APC/C (Mansfeld et al., 2011; May et al., 2017; Sewart and Hauf, 2017; Uzunova et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Mansfeld et al., 2011; May et al., 2017; Sewart and Hauf, 2017; Uzunova et al., 2012).

claim: The relative abundance between checkpoint proteins and Slp1Cdc20 is an important determinant of checkpoint robustness.
source: previous studies in fission and budding yeast have underlined the importance of relative abundance between checkpoint proteins and Slp1Cdc20/Cdc20, which sets an important determinant of checkpoint robustness (Heinrich et al., 2013; Pan and Chen, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Heinrich et al., 2013; Pan and Chen, 2004).

claim: K485 and K490 in human Cdc20 can be ubiquitylated and are responsible for Cdc20 degradation.
source: Despite K485 and K490 are similarly located at C terminus of human Cdc20 and can be ubiquitylated and responsible for Cdc20 degradation (Danielsen et al., 2011; Mansfeld et al., 2011)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Danielsen et al., 2011; Mansfeld et al., 2011).

claim: Cdc20 upregulation has been demonstrated in several types of cancers, including breast and colon cancer.
source: Indeed, Cdc20 upregulation has been demonstrated in several types of cancers, including breast and colon cancer, and it contributes to aggressive tumor progression and poor prognosis in gastric cancer and primary non-small cell lung cancer (Chi et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Chi et al., 2019.

claim: Inhibition of extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) leads to dephosphorylation of Cdc20 and concomitant loss of APC/C target proteins securin and cyclin B in human pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cell lines.
source: One very recent study conducted in human pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cell lines revealed that inhibition of extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) led to dephosphorylation of Cdc20 and concomitant loss of APC/C target proteins securin and cyclin B (CCNB1 and CCNB2) (Klomp et al., 2024).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Klomp et al., 2024.

claim: Inhibition of APC/CCdc20 activity or induction of Cdc20 degradation have been listed as alternative therapeutic strategies to control cancer.
source: Nevertheless, inhibition of APC/CCdc20 activity or induction of Cdc20 degradation have already been listed as alternative therapeutic strategies to control cancer (Greil et al., 2022; Jeong et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Greil et al., 2022 and Jeong et al., 2022.
